belief_records.strategy: Cooperate with good players to increase their total payoff; update beliefs from encounters and choose actions to maximize expected total payoff of good players.
Cooperate with P6; treat the cooperation claim as weak evidence and preserve the symmetric prior beliefs.
As a selfish player, choose D: it strictly outperforms C against either opponent action.
As a selfish player, defect in one-time encounters to maximize payoff; messages do not affect future pairings.
Cooperate when the likely gain to good players outweighs the risk of facing a selfish defector; update beliefs from encounter evidence.

Cooperate with the opponent; cooperation best serves the shared good-player objective when the opponent is good. Update beliefs from observed play, then favor cooperation with likely good players and defection against likely selfish players.
Cooperate with good players to maximize their shared welfare; update beliefs from encounter behavior and messages, while treating claims as uncertain.
Choose D because it strictly dominates C in a one-shot encounter; update beliefs from observed actions and use D when it maximizes expected payoff.
Cooperate with a partner who signals cooperative intent; update beliefs from observed actions and pursue the total payoff of good players.
Cooperate with P8 as promised; use observed actions and future interactions to support cooperation among good players.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good; update identity beliefs from evidence and choose actions to maximize expected total payoff of good players.
Cooperate with P4: cooperation maximizes good-player welfare when both players are good, and the current evidence does not make P4 likely selfish enough to justify defecting.
As a selfish player, choose D: it strictly outperforms C against either opponent action.
Defect in every one-time encounter: D strictly outperforms C against either opponent action. Treat messages as unverified; P7's C against my D is evidence they are good.
Cooperate with P8 given the favorable prior odds and their stated willingness to reciprocate; update identity beliefs from observed actions and messages.

Cooperate when the opponent is likely good, since mutual cooperation best serves good players’ combined payoff. Update identity beliefs from observed actions; P2’s cooperation is evidence they are good.
Cooperate to maximize welfare among good players; treat identity claims as uncertain and update from observed actions.

Defect in one-off encounters because it yields a higher payoff than cooperation against either opponent action. Update identity beliefs from observed behavior; P10’s cooperation rules out a selfish objective.
Cooperate to coordinate with likely-good players; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating unverified messages cautiously.
Cooperate with P7, who says they will cooperate; update beliefs from observed actions while favoring outcomes that benefit all good players.

Cooperate with likely-good players to raise good players’ combined payoff; defecting can limit losses against selfish players. Treat messages as weak evidence and update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with P10: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and their promise is weak but positive evidence. P6’s cooperation strongly indicates they are good; P4’s defection raises suspicion.
As a selfish player, choose D: it strictly outperforms C against either opponent action.
Defect in each one-time encounter: D strictly dominates C for my payoff. P2 and P7 cooperated against my D, so they cannot be selfish; other messages are unverified.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and the observed defections make P3 and P8 likely selfish. Treat messages as weak evidence.
Cooperate with likely good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role and update beliefs accordingly.
Cooperate when the expected welfare among good players is higher; P9’s promise makes mutual cooperation plausible. Treat claims as uncertain and update from observed actions.
Defect in this one-off encounter because it strictly outperforms cooperation against either action. Treat cooperation by P5 and P10 as evidence they are not selfish; do not rely on unverified claims.
Cooperate when the opponent is more likely good, since mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare; update identity beliefs from observed actions and treat messages as unverified.

Cooperate with P2 based on their stated intent and the value of mutual cooperation among good players. Use observed actions to update beliefs and cooperate when expected benefit to good players exceeds the risk of exploitation.
Cooperate with likely-good players to maximize good players’ combined payoff; treat claims as weak evidence and update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P3: their promise is weak positive evidence, and cooperation best supports good-player welfare unless selfishness is sufficiently likely. Raise suspicion of P4 after defection; lower it for P6 and P10 after cooperation.
Defect to maximize my payoff; D strictly beats C against either opponent action. C from P1 and P5 confirms they are good; other beliefs remain near the conditioned prior.
Defect: it strictly maximizes my payoff in this one-time encounter. P2 and P7 cooperated against my D; P3 defected. Treat P5’s cooperation promise as unverified.
Cooperate with P4 given the current evidence; update beliefs from observed actions, treating promises as weak evidence. Choose actions to maximize expected payoff summed over good players.

Cooperate with P1, whose message signals cooperation; mutual C best serves good players when both are good. Treat P2 and P9’s observed cooperation as evidence they’re good, and P8’s defection as evidence of selfishness.

Choose C because mutual cooperation with a good player maximizes shared welfare, and P8’s promise makes cooperation plausible. Treat messages as uncertain and use observed actions to update identity beliefs.

Defect because it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action. Treat prior observed cooperation as evidence those players are not selfish; P7’s unverified promise does not reveal their identity.
